posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Since the game is meant to be cinematic, making things difficult on the heroes would be rather fitting.  I'm somewhat inclined toward specifically requiring the heroes to be paired off like this for that exact reason.  (Those of you who play roleplaying games should be familiar with the maxim "Don't give the GM ideas!")  I also rather want to specify that Legacy should come last in turn order, so that instead of making every hero awesome all the time, he takes until the last hero turn in round 1 to put in his dramatic entrance, and occasionally produces awkward interactions due to declaring Galvanize on the entire following round, before seeing what Megalopolis and Omnitron will do to the heroes that round.

Tell you what...Legacy and Tachyon both have to play cards for their damage, so I'll say Tachy's first (it's only fitting) and Legs is last, so there's an Environment turn in between.  However, Bunker and Wraith should be second and third respectively (this keeps Tachy from colliding with Wraith in case of Throat Jab, though Combat Stance is still at risk), with AZ fourth, for the same thematic reasons as Tachyon (he's participating somewhat grudgingly).  The collisions between Bunker and Wraith will discourage them from relying on the straightforward use of Flak Cannon and Razor Ordinance, pushing them toward different actions and thus making the "movie" less repetitive...certainly, Bunker charging up and firing an Omni-Cannon (ha!) and Wraith using IREP to predict Omnitron's attacks both seem like something you might see in an action movie.

First turn will come soon.

You mean abottom the deck.  Anyway, let's roll the opening credits.

INT. ALDRED INDUSTRIES TEST CHAMBER – DAY

GENERAL DRAKE and several other Top Military Men are supervising the test-activation of Aldred's new flagship military hardware, the XK-9000 ALPHA, which appears as an ominous blue-glowing dome in the center of the lab.  The brass and Aldred's corporate liason BRIAN BLISS are watching from a windowed bay overlooking the facility, while dozens of scientists mill about the machinery surrounding the XK, their purposeful motions reminiscent of ants in a hive.

BLISS:  "As you're about to see, gentlemen, the XK-9000 Alpha represents the state of the art in military intelligence.  When connected to a fully-equipped Aldred Industries Robotic Munitions Assembly Array, ts program will allow it to dynamically analyze the threat parameters of any enemy, and prioritize assets to the rapid construction of appropriate countermeasures, enabling the swift and economical deployment of exactly the weapons needed to end the engagement with minimal loss of life or property.  Our patented Adaptive Interpolation Grid Encasement ensures that the core can never be hacked, either wirelessly or through physical access, and the use of quantum computing technology ensures that the program can handle data in excess of…"

In the back of the assembly, one of the other officers leans close to DRAKE and whispers:

OFFICER:  "You ever get the impression he's being paid by the word?"

DRAKE remains silent and impassive, keeping some distance from most of the group as they ooh and aah over Bliss's enthusiastic presentation.  Suddenly, an alarm light appears on the panel in front of Bliss, but he quickly covers it with his hand and pivots, appearing casual as he positions himself in front of it to block it from the military mens' view.  In the room below, things begin rapidly going to hell; the scientists begin to panic as machinery surrounding the XK-9000 springs to life of its own accord.  Alarms are sounded, the lights flash red, and at last Bliss can no longer keep the situation under wraps.  While the other generals begin demanding answers, DRAKE slips out the door and begins walking briskly along the hallways leading out of the lab, flipping open a cell phone and pressing one button to dial.

DRAKE (into phone):  "This is General Ulysses Drake.  Tell Lt. Vance to be ready to deploy in ten.  Also, get on the horn to the E-R Labs and tell Dr. Stinson we have a situation.  No, I'm not sure…you'd better hope I'm wrong."

DRAKE walks forward out of the frame, which continues advancing along the hall almost as fast as him.  In the distance, from the door he left, emerges the sound of "shatterproof" glass shattering, accompanied by angry mechanical noises, confused masculine shouts, and then screams (the first one from Brian Bliss).

SCREEN WIPE to EXT. EIKEN-RUBENDALL LABS, then immediately to INT. thereof.

DR. MEREDITH STINSON (TACHYON) is on the phone.

TACHYON:  "I see.  Aldred, eh?  You're sure?  Well, can't say I'm surprised,I'llberightoverandcheckitout!"  Dropping the phone without bothering to hang up, she zips out of the room, leaving her lab coat behind before it has time to collapse out of shape.

INT.  DOOR OF CRYO-CHAMBER.

TACHYON zips to a halt in front of the door and raps insistently on the glass.  She then presses the button for an intercom and speaks rapidly.

TACHYON:  "Mr. Frost!  Suit up; time for you to start earning the downpaymentonthatsuit!"

Tachyon zips away, leaving a grumpy-looking RYAN FROST to begin slowly getting out of his bed inside the CRYO-CHAMBER.  His skin is the color of the ice on a major city's less frequently-plowed streets in January, and his chest is covered by a black metal plate with glowing blue lines.  Grumbling all the way, he begins taking pieces of a powered armor suit down off the wall and hastily strapping them onto himself.

EXT. MEGALOPOLIS - FINE DINING RESTAURANT, EVENING

PAUL PARSONS (Legacy) and his WIFE are enjoying a romantic dinner and making small talk.

EXT.  ROOK CITY - WILDERNESS NEAR MONTGOMERY MANOR, NIGHT.

A MOTORCYCLE traveling at unreasonable speed and without running lights turns off the road and vanishes into the woods, improbably staying upright and clear of all trees as it's maneuvered through the forest and toward a steep hillside.  Vanishing into an unremarkable-looking cleft in the rock, it emerges a moment later inside the WRAITHCAVE.  Its rider, THE WRAITH, parks it and hops off, trotting toward the MEGA COMPUTER which fills much of the wall of one room.  An alert is flashing; she touches the screen and it expands into a window, from which several others sprout, showing a series of alarming data: newsfeeds and just-gone-live articles describing power fluctuations at utility stations in Megalopolis, police reports of "developing situations" at several manufacturing facilities, and so forth, all superimposed over a map of the city.  With a grimace that's visible in outline through her mask, Maia wheels and dashes toward the secret elevator into the house; once inside, she presses the button for the Roof.  The elevator skyrockets to the top floor and Maia hurriedly crosses the HELIPAD and gets into her STEALTH HELICOPTER, which a moment later rockets out of an apparent skylight in one of the Manor's many gables.  Flying without lights, it vanishes into the night sky, but the camera pans to imply it's direction - the glittering towers of Megalopolis in the distance.

EXT.  DOWNTOWN MEGALOPOLIS - Evening.

An army truck pulls up and parks.  Inside, the BUNKER suit stands open, with LT. TYLER VANCE about to step inside.

JUNIOR SERGEANT:  "Looks like General Vance was right.  In less than an hour, there have been sixteen more incidents all over the city, concentrated in and around this area.  I hope it proves to be just some Mega U fraternity prank, but you'd probably better be on your guard out there."

LT. VANCE:  "Well, that's why they pay me the big bucks."

Lt. Vance gets into the suit, which closes up around him.  He sits and awaits the order to deploy.

EXT.  SKY - NIGHT.

The Wraithcopter is flying west.

EXT. RURAL AMERICA - Afternoon.

A red-white-blue-black blur is speeding down the side of a highway, effortlessly dodging the occasional pulled-over vehicle.  Camera zooms in and manages to make out the heavily distorted figures of TACHYON and RYAN FROST (ABSOLUTE ZERO), the latter now completely enclosed in his suit and being carried over TACHYON's shoulder like a sack of flour.  While his expression is invisible behind the suit's glowing blue faceplate, the tone of  his voice as he shouts at her makes it clear he's not happy.

FROST:  "WHY THE HELL ARE YOU CARRYING ME IF WE DON'T EVEN KNOW FOR SURE ANYTHING'S HAPPENING?"

TACHYON:  "IFANYTHINGISHAPPENINGWEWON'THAVETIMETOGETYOUTHEREANYOTHERWAYNOWSTOPCOMPLAININGI'MKINDABUSYHERE!"

FROST:  "YOUR HANDS ARE HOT!"

TACHYON:  "YOU CAN DOUBLE-CHECK THE CALIBRATION MODULE WHEN WE GET THERE!  OWSONOVACRAPTHATONEGOTINMYEYE,WHEREDIPUTTHOSEDAMNGOGGLES!"

FROST:  "I SWEAR TO GOD, IF ANYONE GETS A PICTURE OF THIS FOR THE TEN O CLOCK NEWS…!!!"

Camera zooms out.  The blur of TACHY and ZERO crosses the shadow of sundown as it falls across the landscape.  As they approach the western edge of Megalopolis, where the gloom of dusk is rapidly setting in, the shadow of the WRAITHCOPTER can be seen approaching from the darker sky to the east.

EXT.  DOWNTOWN MEGALOPOLIS - Evening.

The hustle and bustle of city life is interrupted by the sight of a huge beetle-like metallic hulk, its body crowned by the immense blue dome of the XK-9000, bursts through the wall of a metal fabrication company on the edge of the warehouse district.  Firing a beam of red energy from its single ominous "eye", the clattering four-legged robot OMNITRON is the size of a small house and crushes cars beneath its steps as it rampages into the street.  Where the beam strikes a car or a piece of electrical equipment, it transforms the existing machinery into an S-85 AUTOMATON DRONE, a skeletally humanoid machine toting a laser rifle.  People begin screaming and running in panic in all directions.

INT.  FANCY RESTAURANT.

PAUL PARSONS is in the middle of a quiet, affectionate conversation with his WIFE, when suddenly the DANGER SENSE sound effect plays and he cocks his head distinctively.  MRS. PARSONS recognizes the gesture immediately.

MRS. PARSONS:  "Oh dear, you have to go, don't you?"

PAUL PARSONS (LEGACY):  "Looks that way.  Always remember, honey, I love you."

MRS. PARSONS:  "I love you t–"

The sound of chaos and screaming has reached the restaurant, but Legacy is already gone, into the bathroom and out the window, his nice suit neatly folded and deposited on a handy fire escape as he flies away overhead.

EXT.  DOWNTOWN MEGALOPOLIS - Evening.

A voice crackles over the radio of the BUNKER Suit as the back of the truck opens and the ramp unfolds for it to walk out.

RADIO:  "Looks like that's our confirmation, Codename Bunker!  Good luck!"

BUNKER:  "Always appreciated!  Same to all of you!"

Stepping out of the truck, Bunker is joined by Legacy and Tachyon zooming in from opposite sides, the latter setting AZ down not quite gently enough to keep him from tumbling onto his face.  A little closer to where the WRAITHCOPTER is just setting down, OMNITRON stalks into view, its domed head scintillating with iridescent colors among the blue.  Behind it march a phalanx of AUTOMATON DRONEs.

Remarks:

I don't think we communicated that well as a team.  I sort of knew what various other heroes were up to, but that was mainly from having played them myself.  So the strategy sort of defaulted into "Build up, deal with threats, and knowing that at some point Tachyon was going to bring Omni down to a vulnerable level."  So, therefore, I think there needed to be a little more side chatter to confirm who was taking care of what, and so on.  Such as, if the group thought sufficient damage was being inflicted whether it was worthwhile rolling out another IR Eyepiece to deck some of Omni's cards, etc.

And given the group's relative lack of on-going control I think we should have taken more steps to ensure a consistent capability regarding that if possible.  Omni rolling out another Adaptive Plating Subroutine in that last round would be crimped Tachyon's barrage, and also slowed up our final series of attacks.  Probably not enough to make a difference, but the threat was there.

And I think the "draw 2/play 1" mechanic makes the villains more threatening.  Much less chance of a "dud play" by a villain such as wasting a healing card or something like Technological Singularity in the 1st round.  It also lessens any attempts by the heroes at villain deck control.  On the flip-side it helps the heroes as well, but probably not to the same degree.

Oh, and the Megalopolis environment did a fair job in rolling out its more annoying cards.

Cinematic Remarks:

One thing to make sure of is to add scenes where the reporters are annoying to either the heroes or Omnitron earlier in the movie.  Disintegrating them in front of the heroes without there being some ironic justice being delivered just makes the heroes look bad.  Especially given that the rambunctous pro-machine protesters get off scot-free.  (Though I guess you can have Tachyon do a modified Accelerated Assault and spank all their asses on the way out.)

Round Four - Omnitron

Play a Card: Electropulse Explosive (S-85 Repair Drone bottomed).

I didn't want Targeting Innocents to see play until there had been an Impending Casualty, as it seems narratively necessary - although in fact, I now think it'd be more appropriate to have one turn of TI without IC, then have IC start happening, as if the Targeting Innocents was getting worse (I had perhaps failed to grok that it does this every round).  Even more ideal would be for IC to happen, then the deck to be reshuffled so TI could come out, and only then for IC to turn up again…but even with the deck burning an extra card each round, that would take a long time to happen.  With a choice between two cards that both would need to avoid 10 damage within a round in order to do anything, I picked the one with the more dramatic effect, even knowing that it might (and did) prove repetitive.  Once Omni's turn rolled around, I had a seemingly easy choice to make, but if I'd realized the Self-Aware Robotics Factory was going to rebuild a Drone, I might have made this choice differently, even though the ominous image of the Bomb rising into view was compelling to me.  Still, I have a hard time getting out of the habit of considering Repair Drone a weak card, a waste of one of Omni's valuable plays, and EPE his strongest attack under all circumstances (instead of just most of them - stupid Hypersonic Assault), so I made the apparently obvious decision.

Round Six oh for the love of Eight - Omnitron

Play a Card: Terraforming (bottomed S-85 Repair Drone) destroys Police Backup and Paparazzi On the Scene, plays S-84 Automaton Drone (bottomed other Terraforming) and That Bomb (bottomed Interpolation Beam).

Writing the Paparazzi's dialogue was awesome, it was very sad that they didn't survive to affect the game in any way.  Overall, the ending was the most unsatisfying part of this game by far…the main reason I say that I'd have to rewrite this "script," if the movie were actually being made, is that basically very little happened until the last round of the game, and then far too much all at once.  You get a goofy picture of Tachyon standing around scratching her head for several minutes while the drones and Hostaging cultists postured and Trains fell ineffectually from the sky, then all of a sudden incredible carnage was unleashed all at once after all that nothing…it would take a fair bit of polishing to turn it into a decently paced action flick.

Still, all told, it was a good first outing for the SCUverse rules, and I'm glad that one of the decks ran all the way through so that the semi-predictability could affect the climax, even if it didn't work quite the way I hoped.
